VM - Arbitrary Data.vi

Owning Palette: Legacy VarMan VIs

Manages VarMan variables of an arbitrary data type; both predefined and user-defined data types are supported.  (*) This legacy VI has a modern successor: VM3 - Arbitrary Data.vi

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

VC Handle specifies the handle of the Variable Context in which to operate on the variable. VC Handle is ignored if name_spec refers to the variable by an alias. See the Referring to variables topic for more information.
The VM - Open Context.vi creates a Variable Context and returns its handle.
name_spec defines the name specifier of the target variable. Usually, this is merely a variable name; however, additional options are available. See the Referring to variables topic for details.
flattened value specifies a value to be assigned to a variable if either create or set value operation is to be performed. A value must be represented in the Flattened-To-String format unless the variable has the String data type (type code is 0), in which case the value must be represented as a native LabVIEW string.
cmd specifies the operation to execute:

0createcreates a variable
1destroydestroys a variable
2set valuewrites a variable value
3get valuereads the variable value (default operation)
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
var type specifies a code of variable datatype. This code is required to perform all operations except of destroying variable. The VI returns an error if an actual variable datatype is different from var type. To manage variables of user-defined data types a type code should be in one of the following ranges: from 128 up to 249, or from 1000 up to 9999. By default, var type is equal to 128.
Exception. You can pass -1 to var type if cmd is get value. In this case, the VI returns a variable value without paying attention to a variable datatype; herewith, var type out indicator contains an actual code of the variable datatype.
dup VC Handle is a flow-through parameter with the same value as VC Handle.
dup name_spec is a flow-through parameter with the same value as name_spec.
flattened value out returns the value of the specified variable if get value operation was performed; otherwise, it returns the same value as flattened value in. A returned variable value is represented in the Flattened-To-String format unless the variable has the String data type (type code is 0), in which case the value is represented as a native LabVIEW string.
err code contains a VarMan Engine error code identifying an error. If no error occurred, err code is equal to zero.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains VarMan VI error code identifying an error if any occurred. If no error occurred, it is equal to zero.
source contains the error description and VI location information if an error occurred.
var type out returns the same value as var type unless get value operation has been performed and var type equals -1, in which case var type out returns code of the actual variable datatype.

 

VM - Arbitrary Data.vi - details

The VI accepts and returns variable values in the Flattened-To-String format, with the exception of the String type, whose values are passed as native LabVIEW strings. For predefined data types, the VI checks the consistency of the data type code and value format, and it returns an error in case of a mismatch.

Also see VarMan overview.
